Details:
- Neovim >= 0.13 highlights the visual selection at cursor position. This PR regenerates the screenshots for failing tests. If highlighting is not relevant, `ignore_attr` can be used on older versions. If highlighting is under test, extra care is needed in order to pass the test on older versions. Adding an extra dummy highlight ensures that the number of highlights is correct.

- See PR [42105](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42105) in neovim/neovim.

comment_regular_data.body: I fixed the failing tests for `mini.ai` and decided to upload. Is the approach good enough?
Hmm... This all doesn't feel right for some reason. Let me please investigate this first myself. There might be some other (case-by-case maybe) ways to make this adjustment less hacky and painful.

> Hmm... This all doesn't feel right for some reason. Let me please investigate this first myself. There might be some other (case-by-case maybe) ways to make this adjustment less hacky and painful.

Yes, of course. I already have all other modules, except the module that needs most of the work: align. I uploaded for completeness.

The following comment in the underlying [PR](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42105#issue-5592544233) might point to another solution:

> Nvim gated the suppression on 'guicursor' instead of the GUI
(cursor_is_block_during_visual(), introduced in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8983): the highlight
was suppressed only when the cursor is a non-blinking block. Remove
that helper too, so Visual highlighting no longer depends on
'guicursor'.

The value of `guicursor` in the tests: `n-v-c-sm:block,i-ci-ve:ver25,r-cr-o:hor20,t:block-blinkon500-blinkoff500-TermCursor`. Indeed, the block is used in visual mode.

As a POC, in test_trailspace, "T['highlight()']['works only in Normal mode']" I changed the value in visual mode:

```lua
T['highlight()']['works only in Normal mode'] = new_set({
  parametrize = { { 'i' }, { 'v' }, { 'R' }, { ':' } },
}, {
  test = function(mode_key)
    if mode_key == 'v' and vim.fn.has('nvim-0.13') == 0 then
      child.cmd('set guicursor=n-c-sm:block,v-i-ci-ve:ver25,r-cr-o:hor20,t:block-blinkon500-blinkoff500-TermCursor')
    end

    type_keys(mode_key)
    child.lua('MiniTrailspace.highlight()')
    -- Should be no highlighting
    child.expect_screenshot()
  end,
})

```

When regenerated with **nvim-0.12**, the highlighting in the screenshots match Nightly...

For each affected test in mini.ai I need just one line:

```lua
...
-- Ensure cursor highlighting in visual mode
if vim.fn.has('nvim-0.13') == 0 then child.o.guicursor = 'v:ver25' end
...

```

> For each affected test in mini.ai I need just one line:
> 
> ```lua
> ...
> -- Ensure cursor highlighting in visual mode
> if vim.fn.has('nvim-0.13') == 0 then child.o.guicursor = 'v:ver25' end
> ...
> ```

Yeah, trying something with 'guicursor' was what I've planned for today. I'll take a closer look at how to best approach this. Maybe there is a more generally useful helper that can be added.

/

> > For each affected test in mini.ai I need just one line:
> > ```lua
> > ...
> > -- Ensure cursor highlighting in visual mode
> > if vim.fn.has('nvim-0.13') == 0 then child.o.guicursor = 'v:ver25' end
> > ...
> > ```
> 
> Yeah, trying something with 'guicursor' was what I've planned for today. I'll take a closer look at how to best approach this. Maybe there is a more generally useful helper that can be added.

I almost finished regenerating all screenshots, adding the following to `minimal-init.lua`:

```
-- Ensure cursor highlighting in visual mode
if vim.fn.has('nvim-0.13') == 0 then
  vim.opt.guicursor = {
    -- 'n-v-c-sm:block',
    'n-c-sm:block',
    'v:ver25',

    'i-ci-ve:ver25',
    'r-cr-o:hor20',
    't:block-blinkon500-blinkoff500-TermCursor',
  }
end
```

> I almost finished regenerating all screenshots, adding the following to `minimal-init.lua`:

That's too much. There is no need to adjust 'guicursor' for *every* test. It matters (currently) in ~50 out of ~5000, so about 1% of all tests. Doing something manually is probably better.

I uploaded the new version.

In test_clue, there are two lines containing `if has_ai then`. That variable does not exist. Can I fix that as part of this commit?

> In test_clue, there are two lines containing `if has_ai then`. That variable does not exist. Can I fix that as part of this commit?

Please not. This is already a big enough commit, which I do plan to trim down later myself (not sure if regenerating screenshots right now when 0.12 is still stable is a good idea).

> > ... This is already a big enough commit, which I do plan to trim down later myself (not sure if regenerating screenshots right now when 0.12 is still stable is a good idea).

What could be the problem, if it works across all supported versions?

> > > ... This is already a big enough commit, which I do plan to trim down later myself (not sure if regenerating screenshots right now when 0.12 is still stable is a good idea).
> 
> What could be the problem, if it works across all supported versions?

Mostly if it is a good practice to regenerate screenshots based on the Nightly version if there is a way to achieve the same without regenerating. I think ideally screenshots should try to target mostly stable release, and only use Nightly otherwise. It is something that I am thinking about adjusting, since there are now fairly granular ways to control how screenshots are compared (ignoring attribute, ignoring text, ignoring command line). Not yet sure though. Hope to take a closer look tomorrow.
Thanks again for the PR! This already did all the hard work. I'll take a look if it can be adjusted a bit further.

This should now be part of the `main` branch as 36f501e5bf2d39fb0c780116db7b566f78fbf593.

The screenshot regeneration with custom `'guicursor'` on Neovim<0.13 does seem like the best approach here. I mostly wondered if it was possible to "hide" cursor on Neovim>=0.13 without screenshot regeneration. Quick experiments didn't prove to work, unfortunately.

Ended up simplifying the helper a bit and use it without condition (the one inside the helper should be enough).
